1.explanation:
1. audits/user-timing-test.js – Contains the audit logic and tests that convert raw user-timing events into the marks/measures shown in the report.  
2. formatter/user-timings-test.js – Covers how the formatted strings for each mark and measure (including the ms suffix, italics, and ordering) are generated in the HTML report.  
3. runner-test.js – Exercises the end-to-end runner flow that gathers artifacts, runs audits (including user-timing), and passes results to the formatter.  
4. index-test.js – Validates the overall integration of the Lighthouse CLI/extension run, including capturing traces and producing the final results object with user-timing data.  
5. lib/traces/tracing-processor-test.js – Parses DevTools trace events into timeline events and applies the normalization logic (subtracting the baseline), which may produce negative timestamps.  
6. lib/traces/devtools-timeline-model-test.js – Provides the low-level model for working with DevTools timeline data; essential to see how event timestamps are interpreted before they reach the audit layer.
1.bug_scenario: In the Lighthouse report’s “Performance: User Timing marks and measures” section on the Chromestatus page, the UI is listing user timing marks with negative millisecond values (e.g. “Mark: -184.69ms – mark_features_unveil_start”). Two of the marks (`mark_features_unveil_start` and `mark_features_loaded_start`) are rendered with negative timestamps, followed by later positive timestamps and measures. The bug likely stems from how the trace processor computes and normalizes the user-timing events relative to the baseline (navigationStart), combined with how the audit and formatter present those values in the report.
